 Posted on November 11, 2026 What Veterans Should Know About Tax-Free Benefits
 S F 
 T 
 L 
 E 
 From Internal Revenue Service
 This Veterans Day, let’s provide some veteran specific tax information and resources. Certain benefits from the Department of Veterans Affairs may not be taxable. It’s important to know what’s considered tax-free, so they understand how to report when it’s time to file their federal tax return.
 Don’t include these benefits as part of taxable income
 VA disability benefits, including: Disability compensation and pension payments to veterans and their families
 Grants for designing a wheelchair accessible home
 Grants for motor vehicles for loss of sight or use of limbs
 Benefits under a dependent-care assistance program
 VA education benefits
 One-time lump-sum disability severance payments received from the Department of War by veterans who separated from the military because of combat-related injuries. Veterans who previously paid taxes on these payments can file an amended return to get a refund.
 While there are many benefits that aren’t taxable, this doesn’t mean that’s the case for all military-related income. For example, military retirement based on age or length of service is generally taxable income.
 Tax refunds and available tax credits
 Veterans may be eligible to get money back or reduce their tax liability by claiming certain refunds or credits.
 Refund related to VA disability compensation. Veterans may be able to claim a federal tax refund if they receive: An increased VA disability rating, including retroactive determinations
 Combat-related special compensation while receiving both military retirement pay and disability compensation Eligible veterans may file an amended return to get a refund.
 Earned Income Tax Credit is a refundable credit that may allow eligible members of the military to get money back even if they don’t owe tax or aren’t required to file. 
 Child Tax Credit helps families with qualifying children get a tax break.
